configurePresets.name: native-asan
configurePresets.displayName: Native with address and UB sanitizers
configurePresets.description: vptr is excluded because it needs RTTI and the core is built -fno-rtti (ADR 0012): left on it reports every GoogleTest dispatch as invalid and buries a real finding. Recovery is off so undefined behaviour fails the run instead of printing and passing. float-cast-overflow is named explicitly because GCC leaves it out of -fsanitize=undefined while Clang includes it: this core turns doubles from JavaScript and from platform ports into integers, so the one class of undefined behaviour the boundary is most likely to produce was the one this job could not see.

configurePresets.name: native-contracting
configurePresets.displayName: Native, clang, optimised with fused floating point — the build the debug preset cannot stand in for
configurePresets.description: At -O0 nothing is inlined, so every evaluation of the same expression is the one compiled copy and they agree bit for bit; a gate and a divisor that read the same sum twice cannot disagree there. Under fast contraction one inlined copy fuses its multiply-adds and another does not, and the two land on different sides of a threshold: round 9 and round 10 on PR #80 each shipped a fix whose defect was visible only on such a build, and CI ran none. clang rather than the default compiler because this is a property of the inliner and not only of the instruction set: gcc 13 emits 98 fused multiply-adds from quaternion.cpp at -O3 -march=native with or without -ffp-contract=fast and never once split the gate's norm from the divisor's on 262,000 inputs at either end of the gate, while clang 18 under -ffp-contract=fast did (6 of 86 at the top) and under its default contraction did not. The flags live behind SPHANORAMA_FUSED_ARITHMETIC in CMakeLists.txt, which picks the instruction set per architecture (x86-64-v3 on x86-64, nothing on aarch64) — not -march=native, which the CI runner's AVX10 CPU turned into a -Werror failure through clang's feature-promotion warning; the gate's 'the build contracts' step refuses a run where the compiler fused nothing, which is necessary and not sufficient. OpenCV is off because the question is about the core's own arithmetic, and a third from-source OpenCV build is a cost the answer does not need.
